questions.prompt: The build prints "undefined reference to 'plan(Path const&)'". Which stage reported it and what is the usual cause?
options: Preprocess: an included header file was not found on the include path
Run time: the shared library was not found by the dynamic loader at start-up
Compile: the function name was misspelled at the call site in the source
Link: a declaration was seen but no linked object or library defines the function
questions.explanation: Declarations satisfy the compiler; the linker needs one definition in the objects and libraries it is given.

questions.prompt: A project has 60 object files at 2.5 s each. A header is included by 18 of them. How many seconds of compile time does touching that header cost (ignore linking)? Give a number.
questions.explanation: 18 x 2.5 s = 45 s, versus 2.5 s for a .cpp change.

questions.prompt: Library sensors includes <util/units.hpp> in its PUBLIC header sensors.hpp. How should sensors link util?
options: PRIVATE, because util is an implementation detail
It does not matter for headers
INTERFACE only, so that sensors itself ignores util
PUBLIC, because users of sensors.hpp also need util's headers
questions.explanation: A dependency that appears in the library's public headers is part of its interface and must propagate.

questions.prompt: Graph: app needs libplan and main.o; libplan needs plan.o and libmath; libmath needs math.o; math.o needs math.cpp and math.hpp; plan.o needs plan.cpp and math.hpp; main.o needs main.cpp and plan.hpp. math.cpp is edited. How many NON-source nodes (objects, libraries, executables) must be rebuilt? Integer.
questions.explanation: math.o, libmath, libplan, app = 4. plan.o and main.o do not depend on math.cpp.

questions.prompt: A test uses assert(f(x) == expected). It fails in a Debug build but passes in a Release build that has the same bug. Why?
options: assert only works when sanitizers are enabled
Release links a different standard library than Debug
ctest ignores failing tests in Release configurations
Release defines NDEBUG, which compiles assert to nothing
questions.explanation: -DNDEBUG compiles assert(...) to nothing. Use a test macro that always checks.

questions.prompt: Two .cpp files include a header containing 'int twice(int x) { return 2*x; }'. What is the failure?
options: No error; the linker picks one silently for non-inline functions
Link error: multiple definition of twice(int)
Compile error in the second file
questions.explanation: Each translation unit emits a definition; a non-inline function may be defined only once in the program. Mark it inline or define it in one .cpp.

questions.prompt: Explain how you would structure CMake targets for a library with one test executable so that the test can include the library's headers without any directory-global include commands, and how you would run the test.
rubric: add_library with target_include_directories(... PUBLIC include) and add_executable for the test.
target_link_libraries(test PRIVATE library) so the include directory is inherited.
enable_testing(), add_test(NAME ... COMMAND ...), then cmake -S . -B build, cmake --build build, ctest --test-dir build.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
